title: Hereditary cancer syndromes and genetic counselling

steps.tx: Hereditary cancer syndromes account for approximately five to ten percent of all malignancies. Recognition is essential for targeted screening and cascade testing. The classic tumour suppressor paradigm requires inactivation of both alleles. **BRCA1** on chromosome 17q and BRCA2 on chromosome 13q encode proteins crucial for homologous recombination DNA double-strand break repair.

rows: Breast (male and female), ovary, pancreas, prostate

steps.tx: **Lynch syndrome** is caused by germline mutations in mismatch repair genes including MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, and PMS2, or EPCAM deletions that epigenetically silence MSH2. It represents the commonest inherited colorectal cancer predisposition. Affected individuals face markedly elevated risks of early-onset colorectal and endometrial carcinomas, alongside increased risks of gastric, ovarian, hepatobiliary, and upper urinary tract urothelial cancers.

steps.tx: **Li-Fraumeni syndrome** arises from heterozygous germline TP53 mutations on chromosome 17p. This catastrophic predisposition syndrome leads to early-onset sarcomas, premenopausal breast cancer, adrenocortical carcinoma, leukaemia, and brain tumours. Radiation therapy should be stringently minimized in affected carriers due to an intense risk of inducing secondary radiation-associated malignancies.

steps.tx: **Familial adenomatous polyposis** results from autosomal dominant germline APC mutations on chromosome 5q21. Carriers develop hundreds to thousands of colorectal adenomatous polyps beginning in adolescence. Progression to colorectal adenocarcinoma reaches near 100% without prophylactic colectomy. Extracolonic manifestations include duodenal adenomas, desmoid tumours, osteomas, and congenital hypertrophy of retinal pigment epithelium.

steps.tx: The endoscopic view shows hundreds of small polyps carpeting the colorectal lining in **familial adenomatous polyposis** from germline **APC** mutation. These adenomas begin early and progress relentlessly. Grasping this carpeted pattern matters because cancer risk approaches certainty without **prophylactic colectomy**, so early recognition drives surveillance of relatives and timely preventive surgery.
steps.say: This endoscopy shows the colorectum carpeted by hundreds to thousands of adenomatous polyps in familial adenomatous polyposis caused by germline APC mutation. The lesson notes polyps emerge in adolescence with near certain progression to colorectal cancer. Seeing this burden explains why prophylactic colectomy plus family cascade testing are central to care.

vis.caption: Polyposis carpets the colorectum with dense adenomas. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Cowden syndrome** is part of the PTEN hamartoma tumour syndrome family, caused by germline PTEN mutations on chromosome 10q23. Characteristic findings include pathognomonic mucocutaneous trichilemmomas, oral papillomas, and macrocephaly. Lifetime risks for female breast carcinoma reach forty to sixty percent in consensus guidelines, alongside heightened incidence of follicular thyroid cancer and endometrial carcinoma.

steps.tx: **Peutz-Jeghers syndrome** is inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern due to germline STK11 mutations on chromosome 19p13. Patients manifest distinctive mucocutaneous melanin pigmentation on lips, buccal mucosa, and digits, alongside extensive hamartomatous gastrointestinal polyps. Extraintestinal cancer risks are substantial, including breast, pancreatic, sex cord stromal gonadal, and cervical adenoma malignum tumours.

steps.tx: The photo pairs dark **lip and mouth spots** with an inset stalked **hamartomatous polyp** on endoscopy, tied to an **STK11 gene mutation**. This triad marks Peutz Jeghers syndrome, inherited in dominant fashion, where pigmented macules plus bowel polyps warn of wider breast, pancreatic, and gonadal cancer risk needing surveillance.
steps.say: The face shows scattered dark freckle like spots around the lips and inside the mouth, with an endoscopy inset of a stalked bowel polyp. The lesson attributes this pairing to a germline STK11 mutation in Peutz Jeghers syndrome, passed down in dominant fashion. Beyond hamartomatous polyps, carriers face higher risks of breast, pancreatic, and gonadal tumours, so family screening matters.

steps.tx: **Von Hippel-Lindau disease** results from germline VHL mutations on chromosome 3p25. Loss of VHL protein impairs ubiquitin ligase degradation of hypoxia-inducible factors, mimicking continuous cellular hypoxia. Patients are predisposed to clear cell renal carcinoma, retinal angiomas, cerebellar and spinal hemangioblastomas, pheochromocytomas, and neuroendocrine pancreatic tumours. Nephron-sparing surgery for renal tumours is delayed until largest lesions reach three centimetres.

steps.tx: Risk-reducing surgical interventions dramatically lower cancer mortality in verified mutation carriers. Bilateral prophylactic mastectomy reduces breast cancer incidence by over ninety percent in BRCA carriers. **Salpingo-oophorectomy** is recommended for BRCA1 carriers between age 35 to 40 years, and for BRCA2 carriers between 40 to 45 years once childbearing is complete, protecting against high-grade serous ovarian cancer.
